analysis: The change set is documentation only: docs/developer/test.md has a date bump (line 3), one new test command at line 1289 (scripts/test-provider-cluster-runtime-models.py), and new prose at roughly lines 1325-1340 and 1353-1356. The prose describes release-publication tests for a cluster_runtime block, a 64 KiB registration body limit, and a model-metadata fetch against a local HTTP registry. It also describes the cluster runtime facts step in release-provider.yml (no secret, keychain removed first, fatal only when CLUSTER_RUNTIME_SEND is true). No executable code, workflow, or configuration changes appear in the supplied units, so I found no regressions against the TB-002, TB-003, TB-011 or T-041 threat entries. The documented tests state they use no network, no weights, and no secrets. The new `cluster_runtime` block sent at registration is a possible new attack surface: the release registration path and its authorization (A-005, A-011) are outside the supplied evidence. Next-pass questions: confirm that scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh and scripts/test-provider-cluster-runtime-models.py exist and match the prose; that the workflow never exposes secrets to the facts step; and that the coordinator validates the cluster_runtime block. The patch excerpt for the second hunk is truncated, but head_text shows the prose in full. These items are verification gaps rather than evidenced defects.
